justification: Two new sections in the conveyancing PDF, a user-facing legal due-diligence document: (A) development-contributions plans named verbatim from the NSW Planning Portal /cp lookup, (B) corridors and land-reservation-acquisition check from the LRA layer 24, SydneyTrain ISEPP layers and the portal /warn endpoint. An LRA hit flips the cover CONSTRAINTS tile. Wrong or silently-missing output here misleads a purchaser before exchange.

pre_impl.existing_data: Phase-0 validated 2026-07-07 and re-verified live this session: /cp at Concord 1456609 returns two plan names plus the HPC block, Bowral 1119594 returns nine Wingecarribee plans; LRA layer 24 holds 5,419 polygons with AUTHORITY and CURRENCY_DATE fields; SydneyTrain_ISEPP layers 1/2 hold 825/800 polygons with agency and defining_legislation; /warn is positive at Goulburn 448547 and empty at Bowral and Concord. Repo grep found no existing reference to the LRA layer, ISEPP layers or /warn endpoint.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If the portal renames response keys or the ArcGIS layers move, the fetchers fail loudly: a /cp body missing both cp and icdp blocks raises and renders Not assessed; an ArcGIS error body returns {} from arcgis_get_with_retry and the missing-features raise keeps the sub-check failed, never checked-clean. Fixtures are recorded live responses, so a drift shows up as a test-vs-live divergence at regeneration, not a silent wrong sentence.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reused: arcgis_get_with_retry (retry plus circuit breaker), the missing-features raise pattern from da_outcome.py, the get_*_live wrapper pattern from get_anef_live/get_bushfire_live, and the /cp parse shape from intelligence_brief._fetch_contributions (PR #460). New: a three-state re-wrap of the /cp parse (the brief fetcher collapses queried-empty and transport failure into one None), the corridor layer fetchers, and the two pure sentence builders. The brief itself is untouched.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Every external call has an explicit failure surface: /cp transport error or malformed body renders 'Not assessed — contributions lookup unavailable'; each corridor sub-check (LRA, rail, /warn) fails independently so one outage never suppresses the others' results; an HTTP-200 ArcGIS error body cannot masquerade as zero features because the client's {} triggers the raise. The checked-clean sentence is only composed from sub-checks that actually ran and returned empty.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend or API-contract change: both sections are PDF-render additions behind generate_pdf keyword arguments defaulting to None, so the free-tier JSON response shape, the pipeline cache payload and the Next.js components are untouched; jest and tsc surfaces see no new types.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Worst case for the reader: a lot genuinely inside an LEP acquisition corridor rendering as clear, or a failed lookup implying no contributions plans exist. Both are pinned by mutation-style tests: removing either raise flips a recorded-failure fixture test; the all-clear corridors sentence requires all three sub-checks to have run and returned empty; LRA wording states map presence, authority and instrument only — the static-claims guard now forbids acquisition-intent phrasing.

functions.name: fetch_corridors_reservations
functions.input: lat and lng of the lot, optional EPSG:4326 lot polygon WKT, optional Planning Portal propId for the /warn lookup
functions.output: payload with query_basis (lot_polygon or centroid_30m), data_currency from the max LRA CURRENCY_DATE, and three per-sub-check dicts each carrying status found/empty/failed plus verbatim items
functions.if_none: never returns None itself; each sub-check that raises is caught and recorded as status failed so the renderer states Not assessed for that check while the others still render

functions.name: fetch_contributions_plans
functions.input: Planning Portal propId as integer, queried against the viewer /cp endpoint with the portal Origin and Referer headers
functions.output: three-state dict: found with verbatim plan names, plan URLs, HPC block and lgaName; empty when the cp and icdp blocks are present but hold no results; failed on any transport or malformed-body error
functions.if_none: a bare {} or a body missing both cp and icdp blocks raises inside _fetch_cp_payload and returns status failed — a degraded response can never render as no plans exist

functions.name: _query_corridor_layer
functions.input: ArcGIS layer query URL, prepared geometry params (lot polygon rings or centroid plus 30 m buffer), and the outFields string
functions.output: list of verbatim feature attribute dicts from the layer; an empty list only when the layer genuinely returned a features array with nothing in it
functions.if_none: arcgis_get_with_retry returns {} on transport failure or an HTTP-200 ArcGIS error body; the missing-features check raises RuntimeError so the caller records the sub-check as failed, never as empty

functions.name: build_corridors_lines
functions.input: the corridors payload from fetch_corridors_reservations, or None when the module itself could not be imported or run
functions.output: pure render plan: tile_flip flag (LRA hits only), alert rows with authority, instrument and map-currency date, note rows for rail and warnings, Not-assessed rows per failed sub-check, and the checked-clean sentence
functions.if_none: a None payload renders all three sub-checks as Not assessed with tile_flip False and no clean sentence — an import failure can never read as a checked-clear result

functions.name: build_contributions_lines
functions.input: the three-state contributions dict from fetch_contributions_plans, or None when the lookup never ran for this report
functions.output: pure render plan: intro sentence, verbatim plan name lines with document links, the HPC line carrying the data-derived commencement date, or the single queried-empty or Not-assessed status line
functions.if_none: None and any non-found non-empty status render the Not assessed sentence directing the reader to the portal or council — never the queried-empty wording

values.value: LRA feature LABEL, AUTHORITY, EPI_NAME and CURRENCY_DATE rendered into the Section 11 alert sentence
values.nullable: yes — any attribute can be null in the layer
values.guard_at: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2322 (each field falls back to a stated 'not stated in the mapping layer', never invented)
values.if_missing: the sentence states the field is not stated in the mapping layer; the currency clause is omitted when CURRENCY_DATE is absent rather than fabricating a date

values.value: HPC Commenced Date and Ministerial Order URL from the /cp icdp block
values.nullable: yes — the icdp block may be absent or partial
values.guard_at: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2278 (each HPC fragment only appended when present)
values.if_missing: the HPC line renders only the fields the portal returned; no commencement date or order link is invented

values.value: /warn item title and layerRef rendered as note rows
values.guard_at: services/portal_constraints.py:843 (title falls back to layerRef with a WARNING log; unknown layerRef values are captured, never dropped)
values.if_missing: a titleless item renders its layerRef verbatim so nothing the portal warns about vanishes from the report

queries: N/A — no SQL changed; all new data comes from live NSW Planning Portal and ArcGIS HTTP endpoints

break_it.scenario: ArcGIS answers HTTP 200 with an error body for the LRA layer while the lot genuinely sits in an acquisition corridor
break_it.what_happens: arcgis_get_with_retry returns {}; without the missing-features raise the sub-check would record empty and the section would print the checked-clean sentence over a real acquisition corridor
break_it.how: _query_corridor_layer raises on a body without a features key; the sub-check records failed and renders Not assessed; the clean sentence is only composed from sub-checks that ran

break_it.scenario: The /cp endpoint degrades to a bare {} response during a portal outage
break_it.what_happens: Without the missing-blocks raise the parse would find zero plans and the PDF would state no contributions plans were returned — an implied checked-absence built on a failed lookup
break_it.how: _fetch_cp_payload raises when both cp and icdp blocks are absent; fetch_contributions_plans returns status failed and the section renders Not assessed

break_it.scenario: Only the rail corridor layer times out while LRA and /warn succeed (observed live on the Concord verification run)
break_it.what_happens: A naive all-or-nothing fetch would either drop the whole section or hide the successful LRA and warnings results behind one failure
break_it.how: each sub-check catches its own exception; the failed one renders its own Not-assessed row and the partial clean sentence names only the sub-checks that ran empty
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_conveyancing_corridors.py -k rail_failure_isolated_from_lra; live-observed in reports/conveyancing/verify_concord_cc.pdf

break_it.scenario: The portal introduces a new /warn layerRef category our code has never seen
break_it.what_happens: A category filter would silently drop the new warning class and the report would omit something the portal explicitly warns purchasers about
break_it.how: fetch_portal_warnings captures every item verbatim (title plus layerRef, WARNING log when titleless) and the renderer prints all items — there is no allowlist to fall behind

break_it.scenario: The lot polygon WKT is missing or unparseable for an address whose parcel sits partly inside an LRA corridor
break_it.what_happens: A polygon-only implementation would either crash or silently skip the spatial checks, and a point-only check phrased as a lot statement would overclaim what was tested
break_it.how: the fetcher falls back to a centroid plus 30 m buffer and records query_basis; the sentence prefix switches to the within-30-m wording and a basis caveat renders

break_it.scenario: Wording drift reintroduces acquisition-intent claims such as a compulsory-acquisition prediction into the LRA sentence
break_it.what_happens: The report would assert an intention the mapping layer does not state — the LRA layer records map presence, type, authority and instrument only
break_it.how: static-claims guard in tests/test_conveyancing_truth.py now forbids the phrases 'will be acquired' and 'compulsory acquisition is proposed' anywhere in the generator source

break_it.scenario: PR #674's fail-open other_instruments capture surfaces the same LRA group that Section 11 now reports, double-rendering the constraint
break_it.what_happens: The same acquisition mapping would appear twice with different wording, and suppressing the fail-open copy unconditionally would lose it whenever the named check fails
break_it.how: the Section 7 list drops land-reservation-acquisition entries only when the Section 11 LRA sub-check itself found the hit; on a failed or empty named check the fail-open capture still renders
break_it.repro: grep tile_flip scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py shows the suppression is conditional on the found state; covered by test_failed_subcheck_never_reads_clean plus the fail-open tests in tests/test_conveyancing_truth.py
